simple.meaning: הֶבֶל (Hebel) appears 8 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a keeper of sheep. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering from the firstborn of the flock and its fat and divine acceptance. The surrounding account also brings the name into conflict and death.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, beginning at Genesis 4:2. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as birth, family, family line, shepherding, flock, offering.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֶבֶל (H1893) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows הֶבֶל through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: הֶבֶל (Hebel) / H1893 is tracked through Genesis 4:2, Genesis 4:4, Genesis 4:8, Genesis 4:9. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

Hebel or Habel II. הָ֑בֶל הֶ֫בֶל, proper name, masculine (perhaps id quod Assyrian ablu , son, COT Gloss ; compare also We Skizzen iii.70 : derivation from I. הֶבֶל not probable) second son of Adam Gen 4:2 (twice in verse); 4:4 (twice in verse); 4:8 (twice in verse); 4:9 , 25 .
